verdict.rationale: Pulley's own docs reference stock certificates it can customize, native in-platform e-signing for documents, and a signature-status view that sits under the cap table's Security Status. Together these suggest certificates are issued and signed against securities in the cap table, but no item explicitly shows a share certificate being legally e-signed and permanently bound to its ledger entry. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that share certificates themselves are e-signed in-platform, evidence of a permanent certificate-to-cap-table-entry link, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, I can issue electronic share certificates that are legally signed in-platform and permanently linked to the cap table entry they represent
